## The equation-of-state limiter: two passes, floors and marks {#sec-ch08-eoslimiter}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- Two passes: one on the conserved state, one on the primitive state. They are not the same operation.
- Switch: `equation-of-state/limiter`, default false. Floors default to $10^{-6}$, $10^{-3}$ and $20$ K.
- Every floor is a clamp, so every floor invents mass or energy. Nothing removes it again.
- The order of the two conserved floors is load-bearing: the energy floor reads the floored density.
- A repair in the interior sets a mark that the redo detector reads.
:::

The outline carries this material three times: as the conserved pass, as the primitive pass, and as a
second inventory's account of both together with the floors and the marks. All three are merged here,
because the single switch, the shared floors and the shared marks are one story and splitting them
puts the reader in two places at once.

### Derivation

There is no derivation for a floor. What there is instead are three facts about the operator that a
reader needs and that are easy to get wrong, and the check establishes each separately.

*The passes do not commute.* The conserved pass floors the dry density first and then floors the total
energy at the kinetic energy plus the internal energy of a temperature floor, and that internal energy
is computed from the density the previous statement has already clamped. `[C1]` reorders the two
statements and measures the result: on three thousand random states straddling the floors, the energy
differs in $2862$ of them, by up to $1.33\times10^{4}$. The order is not incidental.

*The floors are repairs, not conservative operations.* A clamp can only add. `[C2]` measures how much:
on four thousand cells straddling the floors the passes add $4.736\times10^{-4}$ of dry mass and
$1.294\times10^{2}$ of total energy, both strictly positive. Nothing anywhere in the code removes it
again. This is the sense in which snapy guarantees no positivity of density or pressure: it repairs
them, at a cost it does not track.

*The two passes floor different things.* `[C5]` separates them. The primitive pass floors density and
pressure and clamps species mass fractions at zero; it has no energy row and applies no temperature
floor. The conserved pass has no pressure row and floors energy through the temperature floor instead.
Reading either as the other applied to different variables is wrong.

The marks are the link to the redo machinery. `[C4]` checks the three cases that matter: an untouched
state marks nothing; a density below the floor sets the patch mark; a NaN sets the NaN mark; and the
same repair outside the interior marks nothing at all, because a repair in a ghost cell must not force
a block to redo its step.

### Numerical method

The conserved pass is `cons` ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}) and runs in a fixed order: NaNs are
zeroed and marked at {{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}, the dry density is clamped at
{{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}, and the energy is clamped at
{{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}} to the kinetic energy plus the internal energy of the
temperature floor. The kinetic energy there is built from the momentum raised with the cell's own
metric, so the floor is correct on a curved grid and not only in Cartesian.

The primitive pass is `prim` ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_primitive_limiter_ >}}): NaNs, the density floor at
{{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_primitive_limiter_ >}}, the species clamp at {{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_primitive_limiter_ >}} and
the pressure floor at {{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_primitive_limiter_ >}}.

The floor values are YAML keys with defaults at `density_floor` ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}): a density
floor of $10^{-6}$, a pressure floor of $10^{-3}$ and a temperature floor of $20$ K. They are absolute
numbers in the deck's own units, not fractions of anything, so whether they are conservative or
catastrophic depends on the scaling of the problem.

The marks are a two-element device-side boolean buffer, reset at
`reset_limiter_marks` ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::reset_limiter_marks >}}) and read by the redo detector of @sec-ch08-redo. Entry one
is the NaN mark and entry zero the patch mark, set at `limiter_marks_` ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}) by
comparing the density and energy rows against a copy taken before the floors.

: Tests of the equation-of-state limiter. {#tbl-ch08-eoslimiter-tests}

::: {.callout-important title="Check"}
The check is `src/snapy_report/ch08/floors_check.py`, output
`src/snapy_report/ch08/floors_check.out`, 5 of 5 claims passing. No ctest in the repository isolates
the floors themselves; they are exercised incidentally by every deck that switches the limiter on.
:::

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- The floors are absolute values in the deck's units. A deck whose densities are legitimately below
  $10^{-6}$ will have every cell floored, silently and on every call.
- One switch turns on this limiter, the tracer limiter, the reconstruction floors and the species
  clamps together. They cannot be selected independently, which is a design decision recorded in the
  sources, not an accident.
:::

1. **The invented mass is not tracked.** `[C2]` measures it in a synthetic state; the code keeps a
   boolean mark but no budget. A run cannot report how much mass its floors created.
2. **Open question.** Whether the energy floor should use the floored or the unfloored density is not
   discussed in any source. `[C1]` shows the choice is observable; the code makes it one way, and this
   chapter records which, not which is right.
